criteria.demand: Bounded reads set the pace, so callers never see a drain signal at all.
criteria.event: Drain arrives as an ordinary item in the session event sequence.
criteria.mixed: Files and processes use caller demand while sockets report drain explicitly.

drain.instructions: What drain discipline should the socket session contract use?

criteria.later: Build the pull core now; revisit consume when real programs show the explicit closes cost too much.
criteria.now: Deliver the pull core and the consume helper in the same increment.
criteria.pilot: Prove consume as one thin adapter over pull for a single domain before committing further.

sugar.instructions: When, if ever, should a callback-style consume be added on top of pull?

criteria.domain: Give every domain its own drive operation, decision type and error family.
criteria.library: Offer a single generic consume with handler callbacks returning continue or stop.
criteria.pull: Offer shared reader/writer handles with explicit read, write, close and cancel operations.

surface.instructions: Which of the three compared surfaces deserves the first implementation?

criteria.distinct: Each scripted read must live at a different source location; repeated names are rejected.
criteria.fifo: One read site may list several same-named rows that play back in written order after argument checks.
criteria.single: Each site keeps a single row that repeats for every visit; longer scripts are unsupported.

transcript.instructions: What spelling should scripted multi-read fixture transcripts use?

state: The team finished nine full Can programs spanning three delivery styles and three workloads. W1 scans a big file for a JSONL record whose typed id matches, then halts. W2 multiplexes a child process stdout and stderr pipes into one grouped progress record, enforces a cancellation budget, and reaps the exit status. W3 accepts a socket session, counts text and binary traffic, reacts to drain and close, and halts when a handler reports failure. Style L funnels all three workloads through a single generic stream::consume: the adapter owns the loop and each handler answers continue or stop. Style D clones that arrangement once per domain, with files::, process:: and socket:: each owning its drive operation, decision nominal and terminal errors. Style E hands callers opaque reader and writer handles plus read_many, write_some, close and cancel; an empty batch means end of stream, and ordinary recursive functions pump, branch and close. The present grammar parses all nine sources; canlc assert stops each one only at the imagined catalogue entry, either an unknown stream/socket package or an ineligible decision nominal. Established facts: array.fold type-checks $callback handlers and merges their errors; sql::with_transaction together with sql::decision demonstrates decision values; plain self-recursion runs and yields real-can evidence; withFixture filters fixture rows by assertion name and replays them FIFO keyed by per-visit identities, turning overruns into missing fixture and leftovers into unused fixture; opaque givens arrive from the engine and appear inside when rows; failure arms capture values with (as failed) and re-emit them through reconstruction. Fresh observations on pinned Bun 1.4.2: the native source produced no pulls before getReader and exactly two after two reads; cancelling resolved an outstanding read as done without a value and freed the lock; every read handed back a fresh chunk object, slice() isolated the boundary copy, and a streaming TextDecoder rejoined a split euro sign; FileSink.write returned the accepted count yet accepted a write after end without complaint, placing ended-state policing in the adapter; a pair of child writes coalesced into one four-byte read, proving chunks ignore message framing. Non-negotiable limits: grammar stays untouched unless a style earns an extension; only catalogue entries may be added; the lifecycle runs open to closing to closed with a single terminal publication while cleanup keeps the primary failure; owner.ts remains the only scheduler. Observed trade-offs: style E writes a close into each terminal arm, reaching 152 lines for the W3 echo program against 81 to 88 for callback forms; style L conceals looping, cancel wiring and cleanup in native code; style D triplicates one agreement and leaves its exit lookup ambient via a handle-less exit_of(). Treat this advice as input, with acceptance evidence holding the verdict.
